extraction_scope: Worker-6 final mechanism adjudication from paper-local XML, figure captions/images, PDF text, and DOCX supplementary legend.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Pen-BR and Pen-RRR inhibit bacterial translation in an E. coli rapid translation system; GFP protein production is nearly absent in the treated lanes.
direct_assay_types: cell-free E. coli rapid translation system

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=13:Inhibition of Bacterial Translation by the HEXIM1 BR Peptide; xml:fig=2

mechanism_claims.limitations: The paper does not map a ribosomal binding site or molecular target; mechanism is direct translation-inhibition evidence, not structural target proof.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Time-kill data show bactericidal kinetics against E. coli 25922 at 2x MBC; CapM2 kills fastest, Pen-RRR faster than Pen-BR, while Pen-BR and CECP1 require longer exposure.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=12:Kinetic Analysis of HEXIM1 BR Peptides; xml:fig=1

mechanism_claims.limitations: Functional killing kinetics support bactericidal activity but do not alone identify the molecular target.

mechanism_claims.entity_scope: HEXIM1 BR peptides with and without Pen fusion
mechanism_claims.claim_text: The authors argue that membrane disruption is unlikely to be the main antibacterial mechanism for BR peptides because activity requires a guiding cell-penetrating Pen fusion and the kinetics differ from membrane-permeabilizing CapM2.

source_locator.locator: xml:sec=11:Antimicrobial Activity of HEXIM1 BR Peptides; xml:sec=15:Discussion

mechanism_claims.limitations: This is an author-supported inference, not a direct membrane integrity assay for Pen-BR/Pen-RRR.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The DOCX supplementary legend reports a BacTiter-Glo assay for bacterial ATP generation after peptide treatment; it is supporting functional context rather than a quantified primary table.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Only the local DOCX legend was text-extracted; exact plotted ATP values were not converted into database rows.
